hints: Focus on what each chemical test is really telling you about the functional group in G.
No silver mirror with Tollens reagent means G cannot be an aldehyde, so it must be a ketone from the list.
Now check the two ketones for a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group for the iodoform test and for a carbon with four different groups for chirality.
walkthrough:
**Use Tollens to decide aldehyde or ketone**

Tollens reagent gives a silver mirror only with aldehydes. Aldehydes are oxidised to carboxylic acids.

$$\text{R-CHO} + 2[\text{Ag}(\text{NH}_3)_2]^+ + 3\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + 2\text{Ag} + 4\text{NH}_3 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

Since G does NOT give this test, G is not an aldehyde. It must be a ketone.

**Use alkaline iodine to spot the methyl ketone**

Alkaline aqueous iodine is the iodoform test. A positive result (yellow $\text{CHI}_3$ precipitate) needs a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, a methyl ketone.

$$\text{R-CO-CH}_3 + 3\text{I}_2 + 4\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{R-COO}^- + \text{CHI}_3 + 3\text{I}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}$$

So G must contain $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$. This fits a butan-2-one skeleton.

**Check for a chiral centre**

A chiral centre is a carbon with four different groups attached. Draw $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(OH)-CH}_3$, which is 3-hydroxybutan-2-one.

The C-3 carbon is attached to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{COCH}_3$. That is four different groups, so it is chiral. It is a ketone with a methyl ketone group, so it passes all three clues.

options.A: 1-hydroxybutan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{OH}$. It is a ketone so no Tollens mirror, and it has no $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group but the $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CO}-$ group does not give iodoform. Most importantly, it has no chiral centre because C-1 and C-3 are $\text{CH}_2$ groups.
options.B: 2-hydroxybutanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CHO}$. It does have a chiral centre at C-2, but as an aldehyde it would give a silver mirror with Tollens reagent, so it fails that clue.
options.C: 3-hydroxybutanal is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CHO}$. As an aldehyde it would give a positive Tollens test. It also lacks a $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ group, so it would not give a normal positive iodoform result, and its C-3 is chiral but that is not enough.
options.D: 3-hydroxybutan-2-one is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-CH(OH)-CH}_3$. It is a ketone so no Tollens mirror. It contains $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ so gives positive iodoform test. C-3 carries H, OH, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{COCH}_3$, so it is a chiral centre. All three conditions are met.
